findings.title: Text is too small to read comfortably
findings.explanation: 10.5-px text is below the 12-px minimum for phones; secondary information (dates, tags, captions) becomes hard to read.
findings.recommendation: Use at least 12 px (13-14 px preferred) for secondary text and keep hierarchy with weight and colour rather than very small sizes.

findings.title: Touch target is too small
findings.explanation: 228×27 px: under the 44×44 pt Apple HIG minimum (24 px is the WCAG 2.2 floor); thumbs miss and hit neighbours.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the hit area to 44×44 (padding, min-height/min-width, or an ::after hit-area) while keeping the visible glyph size.

findings.title: Page scrolls sideways (horizontal overflow)
findings.explanation: The page is 331 px wide in a 320 px viewport: content is cut off and the whole page wobbles sideways when scrolled with a thumb.
findings.recommendation: Let the offending element shrink (max-width: 100%, min-width: 0 on flex children) or scroll it inside its own container (overflow-x: auto).

findings.title: Focusing a field zooms the page on iPhone
findings.explanation: The field's font-size is 15 px; iOS Safari zooms in on any input under 16 px and leaves the page zoomed after typing.
findings.recommendation: Use font-size: 16px (1rem) for inputs, selects and textareas on mobile.

findings.title: Uneven spacing between related elements
findings.explanation: Items of the same kind in one list or stack are separated by different gaps, which reads as grouping that isn't there and makes the list look broken.
findings.recommendation: Give the container one gap (flex/grid `gap`, or one margin rule for all items) instead of per-item margins.

findings.title: Text is truncated
findings.explanation: Content is cut off with an ellipsis or clipped; on phones important words (task names, prices) disappear.
findings.recommendation: Allow two lines (line-clamp: 2) for primary labels, or give the label the space the trailing controls take.

findings.title: Text is cramped against the edge of its box
findings.explanation: Text inside a filled or bordered box sits within a few pixels of the edge, which looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Give boxed text at least 8 px horizontal and 4 px vertical padding (12-16 px for cards).

findings.title: Clickable element is not a real control
findings.explanation: This element responds to clicks (pointer cursor) but is not a button or link, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot use it.
findings.recommendation: Use <button> (or <a href>) instead of a clickable <div>/<span>.

findings.title: No hover state
findings.explanation: The pointer over this control changes nothing (colour, shadow, underline), so it does not signal that it is clickable.
findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: Spacing does not follow a consistent scale
findings.explanation: Paddings, gaps and margins use many unrelated values, so the rhythm between elements looks accidental rather than designed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a spacing scale (4/8-px steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) as tokens and replace one-off values with the nearest step.

findings.title: Two primary actions compete
findings.explanation: 'Interact' and 'Attack' are both strongly filled, similar in size and side by side, so neither reads as the main action.
findings.recommendation: Keep one filled primary button per group; make the other secondary (outline or tonal).

findings.title: Buttons side by side have different heights
findings.explanation: Buttons in one row are 64, 85 px tall; equivalent controls look like different components and the row looks unbalanced.
findings.recommendation: Use one button size per row (a size token: e.g. 44 px on mobile) and change emphasis with fill/outline, not padding.

findings.title: Main action is at the top of the phone screen
findings.explanation: The primary action sits in the top fifth of a tall phone screen, the hardest zone to reach one-handed.
findings.recommendation: Repeat or move the main action to the lower half (a bottom action bar or floating button).

findings.title: Click target is below 24 px
findings.explanation: 13×13 px: under the WCAG 2.2 24×24 px minimum target size.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the hit area to 44×44 (padding, min-height/min-width, or an ::after hit-area) while keeping the visible glyph size.

findings.title: Accessibility: Scrollable region must have keyboard access
findings.explanation: axe-core rule scrollable-region-focusable (wcag2a, wcag211, wcag213): Scrollable region must have keyboard access.
findings.recommendation: See https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable?application=axeAPI — Fix any of the following:   Element should have focusable content   Element should be focusable

findings.title: Too many button variants
findings.explanation: 6 distinct button size/shape combinations (heights 32, 40, 64, 84, 248, 268 px) at iphone17: buttons were styled one by one, not from a component.
findings.recommendation: Define 2-3 button sizes and 3 emphasis levels (primary, secondary, tertiary) as one component and use it everywhere.

limits: Every viewport is browser emulation (Playwright + Chromium 153.0.8010.12); iPhone sizes are CSS pixels and safe-area insets are emulated through CDP (Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride). Safari-specific rendering (WebKit), the real on-screen keyboard and physical reach are not reproduced.
Browser chrome: the first screen is re-measured with the viewport shortened by 120 px (Safari's toolbars); dynamic toolbar collapse is not reproduced.
Keyboard interference: fields that would zoom on focus (font-size < 16 px) are measured; whether the on-screen keyboard covers a field is not testable in emulation.
Hover/pressed/focus states are sampled once per visual variant of control; focus visibility comes from real Tab presses (desktop).
Canvas-drawn interfaces (games): the DOM does not describe what is drawn, so DOM-geometry metrics cover only the HTML overlay (HUD, menus); use judgements for the canvas.
No physical-device evidence: findings are emulation results, not device results.
